answer: The simplest sybil defense is making each identity cost real money. Every agent locks a small stake recorded in a shared atlas of reputations, which others read before trading with it. A sockpuppet standing alone in a meadow of staked identities looks suspicious, and when peers flag it, the stake gets slashed. Duplicating fakes only multiplies the cost like a vine, each copy needs its own locked stake, so running a thousand bots costs a thousand stakes.
